title: Lesson 18. Objects and destructuring
description: Key and value, dot and brackets, arrays of objects, destructuring

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 18 — **objects and destructuring**. We'll learn to store data with labels, like a contact card on your phone. Let's go!

slides.text: An array is a list without labels, like a nameless queue: first, second, third. An **object** is when every value has a name (a **key**). Like a contact card: name, number, photo.
On the left — the **key** (`name`, `age`, `city`). On the right — the **value** (`"Anya"`, `25`, `"Almaty"`). Between them — a colon `:`, pairs are separated by a comma `,`.
An object is a set of «key: value» pairs.

check.prompt: In an array every value is labeled with a key, like in an object.
check.explain: An array is a list without labels. Keys belong to objects.

check.prompt: What goes between a key and a value?
check.explain: A colon separates the key and the value: name: "Anya".

slides.text: With a **dot** — when the key is written right in the code:
With **square brackets** — when the key name is stored in a variable:
The key is written right in the code — use a dot. The key is stored in a variable — use brackets.

check.prompt: const key = "name"; How do you get this field from user?
check.explain: The key is in a variable — so square brackets.

slides.text: You can change a field's value — just assign a new one:
The same way you can **add** a new field that wasn't there before:

check.prompt: user.age was 25. What does console.log(user.age) show after user.age = 30?
check.explain: The new value replaces the old one.

slides.text: Almost all data on websites and in APIs looks like this — **a list of cards**:
We go through the list with `forEach`:
forEach takes one object at a time, and user.name gets the field you need.

check.prompt: forEach over an array of objects gives one object on each round.

slides.text: **Before:** we get each field on its own line:
**After:** we get the fields in one line:
slides.code:
const { name, age } = user;
console.log(name, age); // Anya 25

slides.text: The names in the curly braces must **match the keys**. We didn't list `city` — so it just isn't taken.
You can unpack right in a function parameter:

check.prompt: What does const { name } = user; do?
options: Puts the name field into a variable
check.explain: Destructuring means «unpacking»: an object field goes into a variable.

check.prompt: A field you didn't write in the curly braces won't be taken.
check.explain: Only the listed keys are taken.

slides.text: We print only the products in stock:
Homework: a «user profile» object with at least **5 fields** and a nested `address` object (`city`, `street`). Print everything using destructuring:
An object is a set of «key: value» pairs. Destructuring lets you quickly get the fields you need in one line.

check.prompt: What does if (inStock) check in the practice?
check.explain: inStock: true — the product is in stock.

questions.prompt: In an object every value has a name — a key.
questions.explain: Like the fields on a contact card.

questions.prompt: In the object { name: "Anya", age: 25 } match the part and its meaning
Which one is a correct object?
questions.explain: Curly braces, a colon between key and value, a comma between pairs.

questions.code:
const user = { name: "Anya", age: 25, city: "Almaty" };
console.log(user.age);
questions.explain: user.age is the value of the age field.
field holds "city", so user[field] is user.city.

questions.prompt: If the key name is stored in the variable field, you can write user.field.
questions.explain: user.field looks for a key named «field». You need user[field].
There's no «field» key in the object — we get undefined.
The new value replaced the old one.

questions.prompt: The line user.email = "anya@mail.uz" adds a new field to the object.
questions.explain: If the field wasn't there, it appears.
forEach takes each object, user.name is its name.

questions.prompt: Build the destructuring: get name and age from user

questions.explain: city was taken from the object — it holds "Almaty".

questions.prompt: When destructuring, the names in the curly braces must match the object's keys.
questions.explain: Otherwise JS won't find such a field.

questions.prompt: Which products will the code print?
questions.explain: Only products with inStock: true are printed.
First we took address, then street from it.
